title: Capacity Corral: Governance for Autoscale Orchestration & OKR Sync (Q3)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and deliver a short, operational governance layer (the 'Capacity Corral') that standardizes autoscale orchestration for Dedicated pools, integrates with OKR tracking, and produces an on-call / ops runbook and rollout gating policy. Goals: reduce manual intervention during demand spikes, provide clear guardrails for burst usage, and map autoscale outcomes to Q3 OKRs for capacity efficiency and reliability.
acceptance_criteria: Governance doc published with clear escalation tiers and traffic corridors
Runbook created with playbook steps for common failure modes and rollback criteria
2 autoscale experiment recipes validated in staging with dashboards showing SLO/CI changes
OKR mapping sheet populated linking experiments and guardrails to Q3 objectives and success metrics
milestones: 2025-06-09: Draft governance proposal circulated for review
2025-06-18: Runbook first pass and on-call tabletop exercise scheduled
2025-07-07: Autoscale experiment A/B in staging (policy A v. policy B)
2025-07-28: Production canary for guarded burst policy
comments: 2025-06-02 — Asha Patel: Kickoff. Collected background: burst failures in May spike, ops pager noise + cost overruns for a small set of tenants. Aim: governance + runbook so SREs have a predictable decision tree.

2025-06-04 — Marco Ruiz: Initial draft includes corridor thresholds (green/yellow/red) tied to p50/p95 latency and token-per-second burn. Shared Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/capacity-corral-draft

2025-06-06 — Priya Shah (SRE): Feedback: prefer duration-based gating (X seconds of sustained 80% utilization) rather than single-sample thresholds. Also requested integration with existing cost dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/costs/dedicated-pools
2025-06-09 — Design review (Liam Chen): Recommended a simple visualization for corridors in Console with colors and brief tooling hints; mock: https://drive.google.com/mock-capacity-corral

2025-06-10 — Marco Ruiz: Updated draft to include duration windows, experiment plan for two policies (aggressive-burst vs conservative-burst), and a Hold/Fail gating checklist for production rollout. GitHub PR for autoscale policy code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/1846
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: use duration-based gating (sustained 60s at 75% pool utilization) to reduce noisy triggers — accepted after SRE review
Tradeoff: conservative-burst reduces peak throughput by ~12% but lowers P99 incidents; aggressive-burst improves throughput at cost of higher rollback probability
Decision: initial rollout limited to non-enterprise pools for 2-week canary to limit customer exposure
Tradeoff: integrating cost signals into the policy early increases complexity but improves decisioning for burst acceptance
risks: Risk: incorrect thresholds could cause involuntary throttling for high-value customers — mitigation: canary and manual opt-out per pool
Risk: runbook complexity increases incident toil — mitigation: tabletop exercises and a trimmed playbook focused on top 5 incidents
Risk: cross-team coordination lag (Billing, Sales) for cost-related enforcement — mitigation: stakeholder syncs and email pre-notification for pool changes
next_steps: Finalize governance doc and circulate for legal/compliance review by 2025-06-12
Schedule tabletop runbook drill with SRE + Support on 2025-06-18
Implement policy A and B in staging and wire SLO dashboards by 2025-06-30
Prepare customer communication templates for canary groups by 2025-07-15
